title: Settlement Economy: production, consumption and trade of goods
about: The implementation of design.json: where the work goes (repositories), components in dependency order, and per feature: the design elements it serves, the code it changes (anchors in the mod source), the data it adds, the features it comes after, its tasks (each todo or done), acceptance and checks. A feature is done when every task is done and every check passes. tools/check_plan.py validates design, plan and requests together.

mod.access: GitLab MCP tools (mcp__gitlab__*); no separate authorization needed
mod.rule: All Settlement Economy mod work goes to this test branch; main stays untouched until the user decides (R3)
connector: add_commit stores content sent with encoding base64 as that base64 text, not as the decoded bytes: binary files (DDS, TGA) cannot be committed through it. They go to GitHub research/economy/mod-files/ at their mod paths (with SHA-256 in its README), and the user uploads them in the GitLab web IDE (R5); the same files also travel in the text patch Tools/GameFontPatch/font_patch.json on the branch, which apply_font_patch.py installs and checks.
old_str and new_str are matched byte for byte: the mod's XML uses CRLF, so the actions JSON must carry \r\n.

A file it edits is written back in UTF-8: a file with Latin-1 bytes (declared ISO-8859-1) gets two-byte sequences. Write non-ASCII text as XML character references, and convert any Latin-1 bytes in a file before editing it (bd217d67 repaired RoM_GameText_Civilopedia_Bonuses.xml).
Verify every commit by fetching the branch (git fetch over HTTPS works read-only from the session) and comparing with the checked local result.

toolchain.about: The DLL build inputs (toolchain/README.md). Given by the user on 2026-10-25; set up in this session's scratchpad. A new session or container fetches them from the same folder and runs toolchain/setup_toolchain.sh.
toolchain.host: apt: wine wine32:i386 innoextract p7zip-full msitools make (i386 architecture enabled)
toolchain.check: Before saying a tool or input is missing, look here, in the scratchpad and in this session's transcript; the user gave the link once.

tasks.text: Safety prediction registered before the mod commit
tasks.note: P29/P30 registered (e1827ad) before the GitLab commit 507d1831. Evidence cb9487b: P29 corroborated (every run completed); P30 REFUTED: median same-seed run time a/b 1.091, all five pairs slower (1.035-1.228). Description: at turn 150 arm a has 5-18 % more population in every seed and more buildings; time per population-turn a/b median 1.030 (0.921-1.112); LQ.F10's P32 on the same measure 0.997. Reading (not a re-decision): most of the extra time follows from larger empires (the goods feed the essentials' happiness and food), contradicted if a profile shows the time in the new code path. Deterministic run (seed 485959733): at turns 100 and 150 every player's Wool, Dairy and Leather equal the products of its pastures and latifundia; the TECH_WEAVING load error is gone. Profile (harness profile build, the turn-100 save of seed 485959733 played 10 turns under each arm's XML): total 26148 vs 24075 ms (+8.6 %); the difference is mostly unit pathfinding (generatePath, pathValid, pathCost, pathAdd +1425 ms, about 9 % more calls), the AI moving units differently; CvPlayerAI::AI_baseBonusVal recalculation +156 ms (0.6 %, 13 % more calls as more goods change); CvPlot::updatePlotGroupBonus 509 vs 518 ms. So the new code path does not cost the time; the games differ. Profile logs not kept (scratchpad). CORRECTION (M41, M42): the reading 'the new code path does not cost the time' was wrong. Code review: LQ.F10's produced-goods term in CvCityAI::AI_bestPlotBuild boosted every improvement giving a good the plot already gave, including the one on the plot, pushing values past the iValue > 0 gate (after which yield boosts are added) and inflating best builds in every city every turn, and ignored the trade tech; each produced good is also a separate CvPlotGroup::changeNumBonuses walk of the network with updateCorporation in each city for corporation goods. Fixed in GitLab f70541a9 (term as the resource code; produced list tested before isBonusNetwork), build 98ef1d5930ae; H16, P33, P34 registered (7d2463f). P33 corroborated, P34 refuted (median 1.059, pairs 0.905-1.112; P30 was 1.091). Remaining known cost: one CvPlotGroup::changeNumBonuses network walk per produced good, with updateCorporation per city for corporation goods.

components.title: Land qualities
components.player_sees: No resource tokens on the map. The land itself has qualities: crop and herd suitability, ore grade and depth, fishing grounds, shown in the plot help and a map overlay. What a tile yields follows its qualities and the improvement built on it; the improvement decides which of the plot's qualities it uses (a farm the crops, a pasture the herds, a mine the ore). Techs keep adding yield as they do now. A city still gains a resource as today, from an improved, connected tile, but the tile's quality is the source instead of a placed token. Forests yield timber through lumber camps (early) and lumbermills (Machinery). Pastures yield every good of their animals: cows meat, dairy and leather; sheep meat, wool, dairy and leather; horses horses and leather. Every good, the new ones included, has its own realistic icon.

resume: The files, not memory or a summary, hold the work. A new or compacted session starts here.
1. Save any new prompt verbatim in requests.json (prompts, and a request with items if it asks for something) before other work.
2. Read statement.md, then run tools/check_plan.py --summary: open requests, design coverage, decisions, progress, the features that can start and their open tasks.

3. Mod work goes only to the branch in plan.json repositories.mod, through the GitLab MCP tools. With a local checkout of that branch: tools/catalogue.py and tools/callsites.py, then tools/check_plan.py <checkout> to refresh status.json.
4. Work only on features the summary lists as able to start. Mark each finished task with tools/check_plan.py task <ID> done, and each finished request item with tools/check_plan.py item <ID> done.
5. New decisions go into design.json, changed features into plan.json, in the same commit as the work.
